subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a Slack-plugin `assistant.search.context` action, and what token/privacy/scope contract should govern event-scoped Slack `action_token`s?
rationale: The missing behavior is a new workspace-search capability that crosses Slack token handling, search visibility, and secret-retention boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API or retention model.

options.title: Add narrow RTS support
options.body: Implement a Slack-owned, read-only RTS action that keeps action tokens ephemeral, redacted, thread/account-bound, and covered by live Slack proof.

options.title: Defer to external plugin
options.body: Leave bundled Slack unchanged until maintainers want to own the RTS security contract or an external plugin proves the shape.

options.title: Revive legacy message search
options.body: Use `search.messages` user-token search instead, accepting that it is not the requested event-token RTS API and needs separate authorization review.

recommendation.title: Add narrow RTS support
recommendation.body: Implement a Slack-owned, read-only RTS action that keeps action tokens ephemeral, redacted, thread/account-bound, and covered by live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent Slack action-parity and follow-up decision history tied directly to this issue.
